one_star_reviews.text: Far from a good experience, if you treat your animals as your family this is definitely not the place you want to bring your baby to for their final journey to the rainbow bridge. From the first phone call I should have stopped and listened to my gut, there was zero compassion, but was so distraught and had read good reviews bar 1 … should have took note of the bad review. When we went and brought our baby to be cremated he was placed on a table and the room was peaceful however all we could hear in the background was people shouting about work etc while we were trying to say our final goodbye. The lady told us after we paid and signed forms that John would drop him home to us next Thursday if we couldn’t come collect which would have been 5 days later which was absolutely fine, it says on their website that it takes 3-5 days.It took over two weeks to receive our ashes back after ignored messages. Messaged again after our baby was supposed to be brought back the week before last. Got a message back saying he would call an hour before he would be here, we messaged back and had no response again. Man called at 5.10pm asking us to meet him in another town, as advised prior we had no way of making a trip via car. He said I thought you lived in such and such a place. I advised it’s clearly written on form where we are from.  the man got annoyed as they thought we lived in a different town and said he wouldn’t be able to drop him to us. At this stage I was absolutely heartbroken the grief process has now been made a lot worse waiting for our babies ashes to be returned. I asked him why I was told I would have him home last week and then again this week and now he is saying he will not drop him and we will need to wait. We had completed all the paperwork so had our address?  The website states clearly that they collect your pet within 24 hours and return them within 3-5 days. 13 days later and we finally got our baby home. They made us meet them at a supermarket car park  and handed us our bag in a paper bag. The certificate they provided stars he was returned to us on 6th of October but in fact it was the 15th of October we received our baby back. My advise is to look into all your options before choosing your babies final journey. My advise to the company is please respect the families and give them the courtesy of basic communication. I understand that the girl who told us we would have him back 5 days later was only new and she didn’t know you didn’t bring the babies back to their families you meet them and certain points of collection however this needs to be updated on your website and verbally spoken to your customers. I would also recommend that you are more respectful and compassionate on phone calls with the bereaved as tutting and sighing and being abrupt is just not acceptable.

Extremely disappointing experience – I would avoid Irish Machinery Auctions

I purchased Lot 3472, a Hyundai Petrol Pole Chainsaw, from Irish Machinery Auctions (IMA) on 13 August 2026 and collected it on 14 August.

The lot was described simply as a “Hyundai Petrol Pole Chainsaw” and the photographs presented what appeared to be an intact machine. There was no clear indication that it was a non-functioning machine, a parts-only item or effectively a scrap-value item.

After collection and inspection, I discovered significant problems that were not adequately disclosed in the auction listing. The condition of the machine was substantially different from what I reasonably understood from the description and photographs.

Importantly, the price paid did not reflect the value of a non-functioning, parts-only or scrap item. Had the true condition been clearly disclosed, I would not have valued or bid on the machine in the same way.

I raised the matter with IMA and was particularly disappointed by the solution proposed by the manager. His solution was to put the machine back into the next auction at no additional fee.

I found this proposed solution unethical and, in my opinion, morally unacceptable, and I declined it.

It did not actually resolve the problem; it simply transferred the problem back to me and potentially placed another buyer in the same position. I would not be comfortable reselling the machine without fully disclosing its actual condition, which is precisely why I could not accept the proposed solution.

I fully understand that auction purchases involve buying used equipment and that buyers accept a degree of risk. However, there is a significant difference between buying used machinery with normal wear and buying an item that is effectively non-functioning or suitable only for parts, without that being clearly disclosed.

For me, the issue is not simply that I bought a faulty piece of used machinery. It is the combination of how the machine was represented, the condition in which it was actually received, the price paid in the circumstances, and the proposed resolution when I raised the complaint.

Based on this experience, I would strongly recommend avoiding Irish Machinery Auctions altogether. At the very least, potential buyers should inspect machinery thoroughly in person before bidding and should not rely on the auction photographs and description as an indication that an item is complete or functional.

A very disappointing experience from start to finish.

Be very careful with Le Creuset refunds and always ask for proof.

I received an item that arrived broken and had to contact Le Creuset three times before I actually received my refund.

The first two times, I was told that the refund had been processed. I trusted the information, waited for the timeframe they provided, and when I checked my account, the money was not there. I had to contact them again, only for the same situation to happen a second time.

On the third occasion, I specifically asked them to send me a receipt or proof of the refund so that I could verify that it had actually been processed. After I requested this, the money appeared in my account the very next day.

So my advice to other customers is simple: ask for proof of the refund from the very first contact and always check that the money has actually reached your account. Do not assume that this level of verification is unnecessary simply because you are dealing with a large and well-established company.

After this experience, I would certainly not rely solely on a confirmation that a refund has been processed. Ask for the receipt and verify the transaction yourself.

Ultimately, the issue is not simply that something went wrong with an order — mistakes can happen with any company. What matters is how those mistakes are handled. When a customer has to repeatedly follow up on a refund that has already been confirmed, it inevitably raises questions about the reliability of the process and changes the level of confidence one has in the company going forward.

I attended All Nations Church Dublin for approximately seven years as a new believer, and I share my experience so others can make an informed decision.

This church is strongly influenced by the New Apostolic Reformation (NAR). Although its leaders use the more widely accepted title of “pastor,” they believe the lead pastor is a modern-day “apostle.” The church reflects NAR teachings around spiritual authority, submission to leadership, and apostolic “spiritual coverings,” which can create fear around leaving NAR church circles.

Preaching and “Bible school” lacked contextual study and biblical depth. Verses were often cherry-picked and interpreted apart from their broader biblical and historical context to support a predetermined prosperity-gospel theology, rather than equipping people to study and interpret Scripture carefully for themselves.

There was also a high level of emotionalism, pressure to serve and tithe, and frequent emphasis on demons, spiritual warfare, and politics. Over time, these teachings and the general posture of the lead “pastor/apostle” created significant anxiety for me around obedience, personal performance, and spiritual safety. They also made it difficult to voice my growing concerns, despite having served as a team lead for several years.

When I did raise theological concerns or question leaders’ attitudes and messaging, I was told, “This may not be the church for you” — a response also seen in other critical Google reviews. While the lead pastor/apostle never spoke with me directly about the issues I had raised, his wife, a co-pastor, was willing to discuss them, although they were never satisfactorily addressed.

Myself and others experienced public correction and pulpit-based shaming, which I found very harmful. The hierarchy here is strong, with practically unquestioning submission to the pastor/apostle and an emphasis on the spiritual “covering” of both leadership and their "Word of faith" teachings. As a new believer, I kept thinking I was dealing with a biblical pastor and a biblical church, when in reality this was something quite different. Eventually, the fruit of this environment helped me see the truth.

Many people here are kind and sincere Christians who genuinely love and want to follow Jesus. The gospel is regularly preached, but it comes alongside a broader emphasis on politics and the prosperity-gospel... teachings that I believe distort Scripture and distract from the true gospel.

Overall, I found the culture intense and unhealthy. The sermons are often hostile towards many groups, including churches outside the movement, with loaded language being used that I do not believe is in keeping with the Christian spirit at all.

If you want to understand more about the theological influences I have mentioned, Counterfeit Kingdom by Holly Pivec and R. Douglas Geivett is a helpful, widely used resource examining the beliefs and practices of the NAR.

If you value careful and contextual study of Scripture, humility and accountability in leadership, the freedom to ask questions, and biblical discernment, this church really may not be a good fit for you.

**1-star review**

Very disappointing experience,when we approached with a damage to one of the gates.

We installed garden gates to both sides of our house 4 years ago and It cost 1650 euro then . We were told at the time of installation that they came with a **5-year warranty**.

Around four years later, one of our gates came off its hinges. We contacted the company expecting the issue to be dealt with under the warranty. Instead, we were told that the damage was not covered and that we would have to pay **€150 for new hinges and for the gate to be re-hung**.

What concerns us most is that **nobody came to inspect the gate before deciding what caused the damage**. We were simply told that the gate must have been kicked in or that it had not been closed properly and the wind had taken it off the hinges. We know that the gate was closed, and we certainly did not kick it in.

There is also something else that we believe deserved to be properly assessed. Our gate is larger than many of the others, yet ours was installed with **only two hinges**. We have seen photographs on the company's own website showing larger gates with **three hinges**. We are not claiming that this is definitely the reason our gate failed, but it is a reasonable question to ask whether the hinge configuration was appropriate for the size and weight of our gate. This should surely have been inspected before blaming the customer or the weather.

When we raised these concerns, the response was essentially that they had "never had any problems" with their gates. However, the fact that they say they have not had problems previously does not establish what caused the failure of our particular gate.

We also questioned the 5-year warranty because, when the gates were installed, we were not informed of specific exclusions relating to wind, hinges, or the circumstances they are now relying on to refuse the warranty claim.

We are not trying to avoid a genuine repair cost. We simply believe that after paying nearly €1,500 for the gates and being told they had a 5-year warranty, it is unreasonable to immediately charge €150 without even sending someone to inspect the damage and establish the actual cause.

We would have expected the company to stand behind its product during the stated warranty period, or at the very least **inspect the gate properly before deciding that the customer was responsible**.

Sharing our experience so that other customers can ask questions about the warranty terms, hinge configuration and what is actually covered before purchasing.

I’m really disappointed with both the result and the way my concerns were handled. I was asked what length I wanted — short, medium or long. As I’m not a lash technician, I chose “medium”, assuming it would be a balanced length, neither too short nor too long.

I believe that when a client isn’t a professional, the lash technician should also provide guidance and take into consideration the shape of the client’s eyes, the distance between the lashes and the eyelid, and the position of the eyebrows. In my case, the lashes are so long that they almost reach my eyebrows and they actually bother me when I look around. And these are supposedly the “medium” length. I can only imagine how ridiculous they would have looked if I had chosen long.

When I told her that the lashes were far too long and uncomfortable, her response was: “But you asked for medium,” as if the entire responsibility for the result was mine. She offered to trim them slightly, but even after doing so, they are still far too long and uncomfortable. She eventually told me there was nothing more she could do.

For €70, I expected much more, especially professional advice and for the technician to consider whether the chosen length was actually suitable for my eyes. This isn’t simply about not liking the aesthetic result — the lashes physically touch my eyelid and interfere with my vision.

It was my first time at this salon and, unfortunately, I would not return.

Avoid if you expect even a basic level of customer service.
I ordered six dining chairs in the third week of May and was told they would be delivered by the beginning of August.

August came and there was absolutely no communication from the company. I had to contact them myself to find out what was happening. I specifically explained that I needed the chairs for an important dinner on 29 August.

Following this, I was reassured multiple times by different members of staff that the chairs would be delivered before the 29th.

Today, 28 August, having once again heard absolutely nothing from them, I called to check the status. I was met with a completely indifferent response from the person on the phone, who simply told me that the order was not even in their warehouse and therefore could not be delivered.

So after waiting more than three months, receiving no proactive updates, and being repeatedly promised a delivery date that they apparently had no ability to honour, I am left without the chairs the day before they were specifically needed.

The most disappointing part is not even the delay — delays can happen. It is the complete lack of communication, repeated empty promises and total indifference when the company fails to deliver what it has promised.

If I had been told weeks ago that the chairs would not arrive, I could easily have made alternative arrangements. Instead, I was repeatedly reassured right up until the last moment.

An extremely frustrating experience and some of the poorest customer service I have encountered. I would strongly advise anyone considering ordering from this company to think twice, particularly if you actually need your furniture by a particular date.
